lines: Plays a recorded kick drum, one press of the button picking which of eight vintage drum machines it is taken from
Each press steps to the next of the eight machines printed on the panel, the press after DMX returning to 808, and the lamp beside the machine in use is lit
A rising edge restarts the sample from its beginning; it fires when the voltage reaches 1V and cannot fire again until the voltage has returned to 0V
The chosen sample played once through, falling to 0V once it has reached its end
Note — the sample advances one frame per engine sample with no rate conversion, so the engine sample rate sets its pitch and its length
DrumsKick.notes: No source is published for this plugin; everything here comes from the panel art, the VCV library screenshot and the compiled binary. All eight drum modules are built the same way: one param 0 to 1, one input, one output, eight lights, samples held in the binary as KICK_sample1..8 and so on. The knob-shaped control is read as a button (a Schmitt trigger at 1V) that increments a stored index 1 to 8 and wraps. The output is the 16-bit sample scaled by 5.0 divided by the sample's own byte length, so longer samples are quieter; that looks like a mistake by the maker and no voltage is quoted here because of it. The panel prints MiniPoops where the maker's own page names the Korg Minipops.

An eight-channel mixer with a level, a pan and a mute on every channel, voltage control of level and pan, an output for each channel and a stereo mix
The signal fed into that channel of the mixer
Scales that channel on top of its LEVEL knob: 0V silences the channel, 10V leaves it at the knob setting, and voltages beyond that range are clamped
Multiplies the left and right gains set by that channel's PAN knob, moving the channel across the stereo picture; at exactly 0V the knob alone applies
Sets the level of that channel, 0 to 1, starting at 0 so the channel is silent until this is raised
Places that channel in the stereo picture, -1 at the left and +1 at the right, on a sine and cosine law that holds the power constant across the sweep
Each press toggles that channel between audible and silent, and the lamp is lit while the channel is silenced
That channel on its own, after its LEVEL knob, its LEVEL CV IN and its MUTE, with the left and right halves of the pan added back together so PAN alters its level
Scales the stereo mix on top of the MIX LEVEL knob: 0V silences the mix, 10V leaves it at the knob setting, and voltages beyond that range are clamped
Sets the level of the stereo mix, 0 to 1, starting at 0 so the mix is silent until this is raised
The left half of the stereo mix, carrying all eight channels after their pans, the MIX LEVEL knob and MIX CV IN
The right half of the stereo mix, carrying all eight channels after their pans, the MIX LEVEL knob and MIX CV IN
DrumsMixer.notes: No source is published; the ranges and behaviour here were read out of the compiled binary. Input 0 is MIX CV IN, and inputs 1 to 24 run in threes down each channel strip: signal in, level CV, pan CV. Outputs 0 and 1 are OUT L and OUT R, outputs 2 to 9 are the eight channel outputs left to right. Params: 0 is MIX LEVEL, 1 to 8 the channel levels (0 to 1, default 0), 9 to 16 the pans (-1 to +1, default 0), 17 to 24 the mutes. Unsettled: each channel is multiplied by two separately clamped copies of its level CV, which would make the response square-law between 0V and 10V rather than linear; the endpoints are certain, the middle is not, so no line claims a law. The pan CV forms a pair of gains from the voltage scaled by 0.2 and multiplies the knob's pair by it, and the two sides are not symmetric about any voltage; only the fact that a voltage of exactly 0V leaves the knob untouched is stated.
